analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown: Positioning, Flows, and Observations Across the Floor (November 6, 2026)
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell 2.7% on the week in a volatile post-midterm tape. The trigger was concern that opposition to data center development could widen the supply-demand gap in the AI supply chain. Goldminers, ACA beneficiaries and homebuilders outperformed. Memory, optical networks and oil had the largest losses.

Prime brokerage: US equities were modestly net sold (-0.4 SDs vs 1-year). Single stocks had the largest net selling in 4+ months (-2.1 SDs), partly offset by long buying and short covering in index and ETF products (+1.5 SDs, second straight week of net buying).

Info Tech was by far the most net sold global and US sector, with selling across all regions at about 2.2 long sales per short sale. In % terms it was on par with the largest net selling weeks on record (since 2016), and 4 of the top 5 such weeks have come in the past five months. US Info Tech net allocation is 14.4% of net market value, in the 1st/1st/3rd percentiles on 1-year/3-year/5-year lookbacks.

Hedge funds sold US Industrials at the fastest pace since April 2020 (-3.3 SDs). Nearly all subsectors were net sold except Machinery and Airlines. The US Industrials long/short ratio is 1.61, the lowest since January 2024.

US fundamental long/short funds cut gross leverage 8.7 pts to 207.5%, the largest weekly drop since March 2020. Net leverage fell 3.7 pts to 43.3%, the 0th percentile on a five-year view and the largest weekly drop since the week of Liberation Day (April 2025).
US-listed ETF shorts rose 7% on Thursday Nov 5, the largest one-day increase since March, and 3.3% on the week, led by shorting in large cap equity ETFs.

Systematic/CTA trend signals are negative in about 60% of global equity markets at short and medium horizons, including the S&P. The desk expects CTAs to sell $28bn of SPX futures over the next week and $45bn over the next month in the baseline scenario, which would put the position net short. The relevant S&P trigger levels are about 7685 (short-term) and 7550 (medium-term).
CTAs are expected to keep buying bonds ($28mm of global DV01 next week, $78mm over a month). In commodities the baseline is oil and copper selling against gold buying.

Derivatives: Thursday saw an extreme vol repricing. Clients had removed protection into Wednesday's post-midterm relief rally, so the market was underhedged when equities reversed and forced liquidations hit hedge funds. The desk's vol panic index jumped to 9.57 out of 10, the 3rd largest daily jump ever after Wednesday's 4th largest drop, and the two-day swing was the largest on record.

The VIX curve flipped from contango to sharp backwardation. VVIX had its 2nd largest one-day increase ever (behind only February 2018). VXN reached its highest level since Liberation Day. Put volume topped 11 million contracts on Thursday, a record.

History after vol panic signals above 9.5: the S&P averaged +4.6% over 3 months (80% hit rate) and +9.0% over 6 months (73% hit rate). The immediate path has been less reliable while the market is still in price discovery.

ETFs: Thursday was the third largest notional volume day in the desk's dataset at $580 billion, 33% of the tape against a 28% average. Friday morning ETFs were 36% of the tape with dollar volumes running 65% above the 20-day average. NDX posted its worst daily move since March 2020 (-5.5%).

Record ETF volumes on Thursday: QQQ $86 billion, levered semis (SOXL/SOXS) over $37 billion combined, EWT $2.2 billion, MAGS $890 million. XLV had its busiest session in over a year at $4.6 billion. Levered ETFs took in +$3.3 billion while inverse ETFs lost $2.2 billion, the widest gap in the dataset.
Levered and inverse ETF AUM is just under $140 billion, down $55 billion over 20 days, and gross exposure fell $135 billion over the same stretch.

ETF rotation into defensives: XLU is on track to beat SPX for six straight weeks (longest since 2022), USMV is tracking the same, and XLV took in over $1.5 billion in two weeks (largest 9-day haul since 2022). XRT had its best weekly inflows since May (+$200mm), and XLP sits just below all-time highs. Six-month lows on Thursday included NDX, SMH/SOXX, EWY, IWF and MTUM.

Thematic desk idea: short the Diversified Staples Basket (GSXUSTAP). The desk says earnings and dividend yield are unattractive against fixed income, growth is insufficient for the valuation, revisions are rolling over, and the basket P/E is in the 90th percentile of the last year. The basket outperformed SPX by nearly 20% in a month and staples have usually lagged over the next 3 months after similar runs.
The desk prefers expressing the staples short delta one because swap financing pays the short at current rates, puts look rich and put skew is near its lows.

TMT: NDX fell about 5% on the week and is on a 4-week losing streak. Semis had one of their largest rolling 1-month drawdowns ever (SOX -28% over 22 days) and valuations are about 50% below the highs. Earnings were a side-show to de-risking and a reset of datacenter build expectations, with investors debating what is priced in for capex or GW builds (more 2028+ than 2027).

The TMT desk's setup for a rebound is NVDA earnings (still to come), less of a financing overhang, relief in oil and rates, lowered expectations and reset positioning. It admits uncertainty about when the market will find out.

Industrials and Materials: Industrials fell 260bps and Materials fell 100bps. Homebuilders rose over 400bps while technology fell over 400bps. Small, highly levered consumer names squeezed (JBLU +30%, DFH +27%, GPK +26%). Data center related names fell hard (STRL, ECG, LGN around -27%, FPS, MOD, VRT around -22%), as did OEC (-26%) and KMT (-21%) on poor earnings.

Financials (+1.6%) and Real Estate (+2.8%) rose modestly with sharp day-to-day divergence between defensives and offensives. The desk flagged negative subprime consumer credit datapoints: UPST noted worsening macro conditions in 3Q and 4Q, and CACC signaled underperformance in lower-score customers.

Shares desk: Friday's bounce (semis up about 3.5%) felt healthy rather than a beta squeeze, with quiet activity. Long-only funds were moderate net sellers on the week and hedge funds were net buyers, driven by Friday's macro cover bid. Next week brings CPI Tuesday and PPI Friday, and the straddle to next Friday's close is 2.48%.

market_movers.rationale: Desk likes shorting the GS Diversified Staples Basket (GSXUSTAP) on stretched valuation, falling revisions and a dividend yield 2.05pp below its 10-year average. This is a custom basket with no US-listed ticker.

sector_views.rationale: Desk likes shorting the staples basket on valuation, rolling-over revisions and yields that look unattractive against fixed income.
Record de-risking and semis valuations about 50% off highs, with a possible rebound around NVDA earnings, financing visibility, oil and rates relief and reset positioning.
Record-scale hedge fund selling and data center related names down 20%+, while housing-linked and levered consumer names squeezed higher.

earnings_insights: Upcoming reports next week (dates from the desk's note, no consensus figures given): Monday CEG, CNH, FERG, KKR, AAON, HRB, OXY, SANM, SKYD, TTD, TTWO. Tuesday CRWV. Thursday AMAT, CBRS, CSCO. NVDA is still to report.
Post-earnings stock moves this week (price reaction only, no EPS or revenue figures cited): VNT +16%, SWK +12%, OEC -26%, KMT -21%.
Earnings were a side-show to de-risking in tech last week, despite some datapoints that contrast the AI drawdown.
UPST (personal lender) noted worsening macro conditions in 3Q and 4Q. CACC (auto lender) signaled underperformance in its lower-score customers.
crypto_views: Bitcoin was at 75,822.07 in the report's cross-asset table, -1.3% on the week and -13.5% YTD.
